newsitem.title: INDIA: Maoist rebels kill 11 in eastern India.
newsitem.headline: Maoist rebels kill 11 in eastern India.

text.p: An outlawed Maoist rebel group shot dead at least 11 people believed to be caste rivals in India's eastern state of Bihar on Monday, the United News of India (UNI) said.
The news agency quoted officials as saying Maoist Communist Centre rebels kidnapped villagers travelling in a jeep in central Bihar, took them to a nearby hill and killed them.
UNI said the incident took place near Dodadih Hills, close to the central district town of Koderma, 130 km (80 miles) south of the state capital, Patna.
The death toll was expected to rise as the number of people travelling in the jeep was 15, UNI said.
Police have launched a sweeping search operation for the rebels in the region, UNI added. It gave no other details.
The Maoist Communist Centre is one of many groups that broke away from India's main communist party in the 1960s.
It is fighting for a radical redistribution of Bihar's land from upper-caste landlords to low-caste peasants.
